chunks: Camphor is placed from the deceased upon the places of prostration, upon the upper chest, the soles of the feet, the place of the sandal-straps on the feet, upon the knees, the palms, the forehead, and the upper chest. And this does not conflict with what he narrated:
ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Kāhilī and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.مَوْضِعِ ٱلْمَسَاجِدِ: the locations of prostration on the body
key_terms.ٱلشِّرَاكِ: the place of the sandal-strap on the foot
key_terms.ٱللَّبَّةِ: the upper chest or throat-base area
key_terms.ٱلْكَافُورُ: camphor used in the ritual preparation of the deceased
key_terms.ٱلْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person whose body is being prepared

ai.seo_question: Where should camphor be applied on the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report concerns the jurisprudence of preparing the deceased, specifically where camphor is to be applied on the body. It identifies several bodily locations associated with prescribed funerary treatment and situates the instruction within a transmitted hadith from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
